title: Intercession of the Theotokos
summary: The Intercession of the Theotokos is a Christian feast dedicated to the Mother of God, observed on October 14 in the Eastern Orthodox and Byzantine Catholic Churches. Particularly significant in Ukraine, the feast highlights the protective role of the Theotokos and is closely associated with Ukrainian cultural and historical identity.

sections.heading: Historical Significance
paragraphs: The Intercession of the Theotokos, also known as the Protection of Our Most Holy Lady Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, is celebrated on October 14 (Julian calendar: October 1). This feast commemorates the protective intercession of the Theotokos for the faithful.

[[coal-in-ukraine|In Ukraine]], the feast holds particular importance, being celebrated with great fervor alongside other significant solemnities. Its roots in [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] culture can be traced back to the spirituality of the [[zaporozhian-cossacks|Ukrainian Cossacks]] and, more recently, to [[defenders-of-ukraine-day|Defenders of Ukraine Day]].

sections.heading: Etymology and Iconography
paragraphs: The term 'Intercession' or 'Pokrov' in Church Slavonic refers to a protective veil or cloak, symbolizing the intercession of the Virgin Mary. The icon associated with this feast depicts the Virgin Mary with an outstretched veil, surrounded by saints and angels, and often includes St. Andrew the Fool-for-Christ and his disciple Epiphanius.

sections.heading: Traditions and Celebrations
paragraphs: The feast is rooted in Eastern Orthodox Sacred Tradition, commemorating an apparition of the Theotokos in the 10th century at the Blachernae church in Constantinople. The celebration includes an All-Night Vigil and is marked as a religious, national, and family holiday in Ukraine.

[[ukrainians|Ukrainians]] have historically regarded the Theotokos as their protector, with the [[cossacks|Cossacks]] invoking her intercession before battles. The feast is recognized as one of the three most important holidays in Ukraine, alongside Easter and Christmas.

sections.heading: Cultural Impact
paragraphs: The significance of the Intercession feast is enshrined in the Pylyp Orlyk Constitution, which recognized it as a day of convention for the Cossack council. The founding of the [[ukrainian-insurgent-army|Ukrainian Insurgent Army]] is also retrospectively linked to this date.

In 1999, the feast was officially recognized as Ukrainian Cossack Day, and in 2014, it was designated as Defenders of Ukraine Day, reflecting its ongoing relevance to Ukrainian national identity and the Armed Forces.

sections.heading: Churches Dedicated to the Intercession
paragraphs: Numerous churches in Ukraine are dedicated to the Intercession, with the oldest being the Holy Intercession Church in Sutkivtsi, built in 1476. Other notable examples include the Intercession Monastery Cathedral in [[kharkiv-oblast|Kharkiv]] and Svyato-Pokrovska Church in [[kyiv|Kyiv]], all reflecting the [[ukrainian-baroque|Cossack Baroque]] architectural style.
